text.p: - Results of local elections in Tyumen, Russia's biggest gas and oil producing region, will influence the country's big politics.
- The Kremlin's practice of cultivating favourites among the regional political elites has led to the creation of alternative power centres to Moscow and to serious territorial economic disbalance.
- According to Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, the new loan rating acquired by Russia will give it better access to world financial markets.
- Russian security supremo Alexander Lebed's meeting with NATO leaders in Brussels has not helped solve disagreements over the alliance's plans for eastward expansion.
- The long-expected radical army reform in Russia is likely to turn into a big political battle.
- Speculation about President Yeltsin's health destabilises financial markets and diverts public attention from real economic problems.
- Russia is like a ship without a captain. Power paralysis has developed because of the president's ill health, the newspaper says.
- Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov has once again dismissed rumours that he is going to fight for the presidency. "I am in the president's team and I will stay with him to the end", he says in an interview.
